findings.explanation: The repo root is the reusable module itself, and it currently has zero `terraform { required_providers {...} } }` block (terraform.tf was deleted per the pending git diff). HLD_TF_001/HLD_TF_002/HLD_TF_044/HLD_TF_054 all report 0 failures anyway, because those checks only fail on an existing `terraform`/`provider_requirement` resource with a bad attribute value — they cannot fail on the resource type being entirely absent from a directory. The scan's 'passed: 114' count is satisfied by the one surviving `terraform` block in example/examplea/terraform.tf, which is a separate root configuration for the example, not the module. Any consumer pulling this module via `module.source` gets no enforced minimum Google provider version or Terraform version, so a future provider release that changes an attribute this module relies on (worker_config.no_external_ip, network_config.peered_network) could silently break consumers with nothing to catch it.
findings.remediation: Restore terraform.tf at the module root with the required_providers/required_version block (mirrors the version already validated in example/examplea/terraform.tf: google ~> 7.31.0, required_version >= 1.5.0).
findings.title: Module root has no terraform/required_providers block — terraform.tf was deleted

suggested_policies.rationale: google_cloudbuild_trigger has only 2 policies in coverage_by_type (HLD_GCP_191 default-SA, HLD_GCP_192 comment-control) — no check on the inline build.step.name builder image itself. This repo's own trigger uses `name = "gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker"` with no tag or digest, which resolves to the mutable :latest manifest. This mirrors the exact risk already codified for Cloud Run v2 jobs (HLD_GCP_304/HLD_GCP_265) — a repointed tag gets code execution under the trigger's service account — but no equivalent rule exists for Cloud Build trigger build steps. Implemented upstream as HLD_GCP_460 (policy + fixture + test, committed directly to main in the local JamesWoolfenden/holden fork clone, not pushed/PR'd per user instruction).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_460
name: Cloud Build inline build steps must not use unpinned builder images
principle: supply-chain
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  An inline build { step { name = ... } } block references a builder image by
  a mutable tag (or no tag at all, which resolves to :latest). Anyone with
  push access to the referenced repository, or an attacker who compromises
  it, can repoint the tag to a different image without changing the
  Terraform. Because the build runs under the trigger's service account, a
  repointed builder image gets arbitrary code execution with that account's
  permissions. Pinning to an immutable sha256 digest removes the mutable
  indirection.
remediation: |
  Pin each build step's image to its digest:

  ```hcl
  build {
    step {
      name = "gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker@sha256:<digest>"
      args = ["build", "-t", "gcr.io/${var.project_id}/app", "."]
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_cloudbuild_trigger:
    path: build.step.name
    type: container_image_digest
